chapters.title: is there a lifetime waiting for us in a world where I am yours (buried feelings grow in a good dream)
chapters.html:
Mydeimos of Castrum Kremnos is not privy to strange dreams. He has heard of rumors that those faithful to Oronyx held a belief that dreams were a medium for the Veil of Evernight to impart some sort of divination or prophecy. Some say it was a gift, bittersweet illusions that tell of lifetimes, of desires, and of regrets left unfulfilled. He knows not to trust easily on baseless rumors, yet a part of him is skeptical. His dreams, no matter how nonsensical it was, always left him with a sense of emptiness he could not explain nor reason. Like a breeze gently caressing his face, in hopes of bringing comfort, yet so fleeting that he was only left behind to yearn for more. 

The first instance that Oronyx blesses him with their gift was when queen Gorgo, his mother, and king Eurypon, his father, regaled him with the story of his parent’s first meeting.

“Your father and I met during the festival of Kremnos.” Gorgo tells him with a wisp of nostalgia on her voice, as she braids a strand of his hair, lounging in the kline overlooking the window of their library. “My spear clashed against your father’s blade for ten rounds, yet our duel ultimately ended in a draw.” 

“We found ourselves equals, and there I asked your mother to be my queen, for there was no one more deserving than her.” A voice continues his mother’s story. Mydeimos raises his head near the window, finding his father leaning against the edge, with the same wisp of nostalgia from his mother on Eurypon’s smile. 

Gorgo chuckles as she finishes the braid on Mydeimos’ hair. She clasped her palms between his cheeks and placed her forehead on his. “You, too, shall one day find your equal, my dearest Mydeimos, my son.” 

Equal

He drifts to sleep in his mother’s arms as the desire of finding the one who shall stand by his side, guarding his back, takes root upon his anticipatory heart. What would they be like? Would they glance at him, and already know what is on his heart? How shall they fight in battle? Will they carry a sword or a lance? 

He opens his eyes to a battlefield. A dream. Mydeimos mused as his eyes inspected his surroundings. The sound of steel clashing against steel rings on his ears, though there was no sight of where the fight was or who was fighting. Yet, he feels his heart speed fast. He knows this is just a dream yet he feels his whole being reverberate, as if his own soul is calling out to the sound of clashes. He tries to move forward, yet he finds his feet stuck to the ground.

Mydeimos closes his eyes in an attempt to pinpoint the exact location of the clash, yet it feels as if it is all around him. Then, he hears it.

Unbridled laughter. So unbearably taunting, so teasing, yet so irrevocably radiant.

He snaps his eyes wide open. His heart beats faster as the laughter continues to ring alongside clashes of steel. He does not know, yet he knows. He knows that gauntlets were meeting against the edge of a greatsword. He knows that this duel has been nearing its tenth day. He knows what will come. He knows that words that will goad him – goaded him, will follow. And then a reply would come next, equally taunting. 

Badump. Badump. Badump. 
Yet it does not come. The ringing of laughter starts to feel distant just as the sounds of clashes start to fade. As if a ship in the ocean starts to sail, ne’er to dock again. Just as the eyes of Aquila shutting closed, ne’er to open again. Just as Kephale slumbers for the sake of the world, ne’er to wake again.

Wait!

Mydeimos wants to shout, yet he finds his voice lost. He tries to command his body to move, yet only finds his arms to be able to move. His surroundings start to distort, a heavy fog clouding his visions. Amidst the sea of fog is a light so blue, so warm, yet fading. Mydeimos stretches his arms towards the light, as if trying to clutch a dying star. As if trying to cusp a wisp of hair he knows is snow-like white. Yet it does nothing, as the light dims. 

He wakes. He wakes with his arms stretched above. “Oh my dear son, why are you crying?” His mother, clasping his outstretched hand, asks concerned. 

Ah. That’s right. He fell asleep on his mother’s lap, listening to the tale of his parents’ first duel. 

Crying? Mydeimos brought his other arms towards his face, and he found it wet from tears. “Mother. I–” Mydeimos starts, and stops at the same time. His dream has already faded away from his eyes. As if he did not dream at all. The evidence he did – his tears – were already drying, and his heart had already calmed down. “I don’t…know” He finishes. He hears the sense of loss in his tone. He knows his mother hears it too. 

He keeps the sound of laughter locked inside his heart. A sound so precious yet fleeting.

Sometimes, he dreams of fire. A fire so unyielding towards fate consuming the library of Garbaniphoro, leaving nothing but ashes in its wake. He wakes with the feeling of grief. He runs towards the entrance of the library, anxiety mourning in his heart, only to find the shelves untouched by flame. Other times, he dreams of a greatsword with a light so blinding, piercing his tenth thoracic vertebrae, and he feels a touch so scalding behind him, caressing his face. A love that still loved even when the tip of the blade kissed his back.

And sometimes, when Oronyx is kind, he dreams of laying down amidst golden wheat fields under a blue sky enlightened by the sun. With another weight on his side he knows in that dream is someone he so dearly cherishes. Yet just like the first instance, just like all his other dreams, his mind forgets.

Though his mind forgets – his body, his heart, and his soul – remembers. In the way he fights in the battlefield, glancing towards his back subconsciously, only to be greeted with the absence in his side, and in his heart. On the way he spends his time in the library as if the doors will open abruptly, and a figure will emerge. 

When the mobile fortress of Castrum Kremnos situated itself near Okhema, Mydeimos gazes upon the slumbering Kephale, bearing the weight of the dawn on their back. He has heard tales of Nikador’s nemesis. 

Kephale, the titan of creation, the father of all heroes, the symbol of Deliverance. A stature so tall, so unyielding with the weight of the world on their shoulder. The origin of Kephale is known to all, from one of the eyes along with the lightning spear of Aquila thrown against the spine of Georios, came the birth of the worldbearer. They grew into a giant, greater than Aquila, sprouted hands that touched the domain of sky, and legs to stride across the earth, with hair touched by clouds and eyes painted by the sky.

Mydeimos felt his heart grew heavy when he first heard the origin of Kephale. If he closed his eyes, he could picture it. An indomitable figure, with snow-like hair and eyes glimmering with the sapphire of the skies. A smile so gentle and a gaze so soft it was almost teasing. Yet before the image could solidify, it faded just as abruptly, and he was left clasping of what remained. 

The lightning spear of Aquila, reforged by the river of souls, had become the lance of fury, tempered and wielded by Nikador, the patron titan of Castrum Kremnos. 

How ironic. Mydeimos thought with his hands crossed, still gazing upon Kephale. If Aquila had never been blinded by pride, would Kephale still have been born? Would the lightning spear not be tempered into the lance of fury by Nikador?

One would not be whole without the other. So similar in nature, yet so different their gazes upon the world.

Strife is the agony that civilizations need to prosper, to grow, and to overcome. Yet unlike Nikador, Kephale guided their creations just like a gentle parent. However, too much strife breeds unnecessary bloodshed, and too much guidance results in dependence. There was no right or wrong between the ideals of the two divine beings, yet never to be truly understood by mortals. The tales of rivalry between them were known through the whole corners of Amphoreus. Thus, came the eternal reenactment of their rivalry. From the coronal phoenix and its natural enemy, the golden-clawed eagle, to the gorgo lion and the oryx, to the city-state of Okhema and Castrum Kremnos, to Mydeimos and—

“Your highness! There you are.”
His thoughts were cut by a familiar voice shouting his title. He tore his gaze from Kephale and glanced towards the light pink-haired approaching figure.

“Hephaestion. What is it?” Mydeimos asked. The figure, Hephaestion, nearing Mydeimos, chuckled softly. “You seemed so deep in thought that I cannot help but approach you.” 

Hephaestion sat in the kline next to the window, where Mydeimos leaned against. “What is on your mind, my dear friend?” 

Mydeimos turned his gaze back to Kephale, and stayed silent for a long time that Hephaestion almost thought that he fell asleep. “Merely reminiscing of tales of the worldbearer, nothing more.” Mydeimos replied suddenly, his voice contemplating. Yet Hephaestion, a friend who knew Mydeimos for a long time, notes the hint of wistfulness in his highness’ voice.

“Are you planning to become a priest of Kephale?” Hephaestion teased him, while tilting his head. Hearing a scoff for a reply, he laughed. “Jesting, I am merely jesting.” 

Mydeimos, remembering the trails of his thought, narrowed his golden eyes. To Mydeimos and who? He tries to remember, tries to burrow his previous thoughts, yet he knows from his dreams that this too shall pass, like scoping sand in his palms, only for it to escape within his grasp. He closed his eyes and heaved a sigh as he leaned his head towards the window, letting the dimmed light of Kephale caress his face. Like a lover. 

He dreams of a bird made of wax, something like a candle, flying towards the sun. Yet, before it neared the blazing star, the wings melted, and the bird came crashing down, o’er the top of a hill amidst golden wheat fields. He ran towards it, as fast as he could in a dreamscape, but when he arrived, not even a single feather remained from the bird. A single cinder left behind leaving him only to be picked up by the wind that caressed him before it, too, left. 

Such cruel fate, could you accept, Mydeimos? 

Mydeimos has heard of the prophesied deliverer. A gray-haired, golden-eyed deliverer. Someone from beyond the sky who will save Amphoreus. Deliverer. He tastes the hint of sourness when the thought of calling them their title enters his mind. A feeling of wrongness. A hint of elegiac grief. A quiet resignation. As if he was standing in front of a funeral pyre, still burning always burning. Mourning. Yet there was no funeral before him, no one to mourn for, no one to miss.

When Mydeimos strides the roads of Marmoreal Market, he finds his feet guiding himself. As if his body knew every corner, every crevice, and every rooftop. As if he had been here before. Yet, as the thought comes to his mind, the feeling of knowing leaves him behind. He does not know whether he is in a dream or in reality. 

Focus. He shakes his head as his eyes closed. But in doing so, a shop catches his eyes. An ancient artifact shop. He sees the owner rummaging from the store’s items, and a fleeting image comes through his mind. Of another figure, conversing with the owner about antiques before the figure catches him in his peripherals and waves his hands with a smile. The thought leaves him behind quickly before he could even see clearly the visage of that figure.

He falls asleep in the grass of the Garden of Life, playing with the chimeras. Just like any other times, he dreams. In his vision, a blue beetle pushes a rock towards the top of a tree, only to fall back again, and continue.

Again. Again, and Again. In his dreams, the beetle continues fighting fate. 33,550,336 times.

He wakes to someone besides him, playing with the chimeras, humming a song. He hears the tone full of melancholy and fragility, a dirge hummed by a low, trembling voice.
He tilts his head towards the side and sees a pink-haired girl sitting besides him, wearing a purple dress. “You must be…” His voice came out raspy from sleep and he clears his throat as he sat up

The humming came to an abrupt stop as the girl glances to his direction and he is greeted by eyes as blue as the sky. 

“Hi! It was such a cute scene that I could not help but approach!” The girl smiles as she continues petting the gray and orange-furred chimeras beside them. 
Cyrene, the pink-haired companion of the deliverer. Once again, that feeling rears back to him. He shuts his eyes off hoping to clear his head. He opens his eyes again and sees Cyrene watching him. He thought he saw a hint of grief within those eyes, but before he could ask her about it, “It’s such a nice pleasure to meet you here, your highness.” Once again. The girl continues with a smile on her face and a twinkle in her eyes, leaving the words unsaid, cutting off Mydeimos’ thoughts.

Mydeimos nods his head towards her as a gesture of acknowledgment. “The pleasure is mine.” 

His gaze turns towards the slumbering Kephale, ever-bearing the dawn on their shoulders. The sound of comfortable silence festers for a time before the figure beside him says her mind.

“Kephale, the symbol of deliverance and the father of heroes, bearing the dawn on their shoulder, to leave a glimmer of light upon Okhema.” Cyrene voiced out besides him, her tone as melancholic as when she hummed. He tears his gaze away from the slumbering titan towards her. Her hands have already stopped petting the two chimeras, clutching a book on her chest. 

She closes her eyes, as if the mere act of gazing upon the titan breaks her heart, “If Kephale ever forgets, then who shall remember?” She asks no one, for no one has an answer. Her hands clutched tightly on the book she holds. 
Mydeimos finds himself unable to voice out his thoughts, feeling a lump within his throat. If Kephale never forgets, do you still remember the ones who won’t reach the dawn?

“The memories of Strife are defiant and persistent.” She opens her eyes slowly to look him in the eye, “So why don’t I regale you of the story of the sun who blazed so brightly before the pale dawn broke?” Cyrene finishes with a melancholic smile on her face, as she offers the book towards him. 

He has never loved himself, 
Why would he love this world?

When it is time for him to depart, he offers gratitude towards the girl. He does not know if the gratitude is for the story, or for something else. Only the smile of the pink-haired girl and her departing words he remembers.

Let us end this story the way we want it to end. A romantic, tearful end. 

When he enters the library of Garbaniphoro, he is met with the figure of his mother reading. When she hears him enter, she looked up from her book ready to welcome her son home, and is met with–

“Mydeimos…”

“Oh, mother…” Before he could even approach her, his legs give out, and he collapses upon the floor. Hurried steps approach him, collapsing in front of him, holding him close, whispering words that he cannot hear.
Mydei does not know what face his mother is making. All he could think of–

A promise that was not fulfilled. 

A tale so cruel, of a flame that burned a million times.

A lily blooms on his feet.

He dreams once again. This time, he dreams of lifetimes. 

He dreams of being a performer singing in front of a crowd, and coming home to a warm embrace that smelled like the wind.

He dreams of waking to a tight hold, with sunlight seeping from the window, lighting the white hair of the man sleeping beside him, waiting for the eyes he knows are blue to wake.

He dreams of walking beside the shore, with the man holding his hands, his head thrown back into a laugh so joyously radiant, with other figures in front of them he knows are the other chrysos heirs.

He dreams of holding a bundle of joy in his arms, a mix of his own and the man's.

He dreams of falling, catching someone falling from the sky. 

Mydei opens his eyes, standing beneath the gaze of Kephale, his arms crossed. He sweeps his gaze towards the slumbering titan. A trembling sigh escapes him, before a smile breaks on his face he knows is filled with a myriad of emotions. 

Bittersweet longing, and a defiant hope fills his whole being. 

He feels the sudden breeze beside him. He feels it hold his waist, he feels it in his shoulder. He could almost, almost, hear the quiet laughter. He could almost feel a palm on his back, guarding him. Guarding his tenth thoracic vertebrae. He could almost picture the gaze of the eyes of the person he held a promise. Gentle, melancholic, yet filled with light. He closes his eyes, hoping to never forget the fleeting touch he knows from his fleeting dreams. From millions of lifetimes. He opens his eyes filled with a blazing fire of determination.  

See you around, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae.

The breeze leaves him behind, with a whisper he does not hear.

It’s a date, Mydeimos. 

Mydei sets his eyes towards tomorrow.
